architecture_decisions.recommendation: Enhanced navigation structure with workspace and organization switchers in the sidebar
architecture_decisions.rationale: The previous navigation only had a user dropdown. The new design adds dedicated workspace (project) and organization switchers with settings access, improving discoverability and reducing clicks. This creates a clear hierarchy: workspace → organization → account.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the old single dropdown approach
Adding switchers only to the top breadcrumb

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Lazy loading of projects and organizations with error handling and retry logic
architecture_decisions.rationale: Projects and organizations are loaded only when their respective dropdowns are opened, reducing initial page load. Error states are handled gracefully with retry buttons. This prevents unnecessary API calls while maintaining good UX.
alternatives_considered: Loading all data upfront on page load

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Local state management with React hooks for dropdowns and modals
architecture_decisions.rationale: Used useState for dropdown open states, loading states, and modal visibility. useTransition for navigation transitions to prevent UI blocking. This keeps the component self-contained without requiring global state.
alternatives_considered: Using Zustand or Redux for global state

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added new translation keys and updated existing ones across all 14 supported languages
architecture_decisions.rationale: All new UI text (like 'Change workspace', 'Change organization') needed translation. Also fixed existing translation inconsistencies (e.g., 'Etwas zufrieden' → 'Einigermaßen zufrieden' in German).
alternatives_considered: Adding translations only for major languages

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added proper ARIA labels and keyboard navigation support
architecture_decisions.rationale: Dropdown triggers have aria-label attributes for screen readers when collapsed. Focus management uses focus-visible rings. Button elements are used instead of divs for clickable items.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Consistent styling patterns and icon usage across navigation elements
architecture_decisions.rationale: All switchers use the same visual pattern: icon + label + chevron. Consistent spacing, hover states, and loading indicators. Updated project-breadcrumb to use FoldersIcon instead of HotelIcon for consistency.
alternatives_considered: Different styling for each switcher type

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Comprehensive error handling with user-friendly messages and retry options
architecture_decisions.rationale: Network failures when loading projects/organizations show descriptive errors with 'Try again' buttons. Uses getFormattedErrorMessage utility to handle different error formats. Prevents silent failures.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Prop drilling additional data from parent layout to navigation component
architecture_decisions.rationale: EnvironmentLayout passes organizationProjectsLimit, isMultiOrgEnabled, isLicenseActive, and isAccessControlAllowed to MainNavigation. This allows the navigation to make permission-based decisions without additional API calls.

tickets.title: Enhanced sidebar navigation with workspace and organization switchers
tickets.description: Add dropdown switchers for workspace (project) and organization in the main sidebar with settings access, lazy loading, and error handling

tickets.title: Internationalization updates for new navigation features
tickets.description: Add translation keys for new UI text and fix existing translation inconsistencies across all 14 supported languages

tickets.title: Prop updates and icon consistency
tickets.description: Update EnvironmentLayout to pass additional props to MainNavigation and ensure consistent icon usage across navigation components

implementation_summary:
The implementation enhances the navigation user experience by restructuring the sidebar to include dedicated workspace (project) and organization switchers alongside the existing user dropdown. This creates a clear hierarchical navigation pattern where users can switch between different contexts without leaving their current page.

Key patterns used include lazy loading with useEffect hooks that trigger data fetching only when dropdowns are opened, comprehensive error handling with user-friendly retry options, and consistent visual design across all navigation elements. The implementation leverages existing modal components (CreateProjectModal, CreateOrganizationModal, ProjectLimitModal) for creating new entities, maintaining consistency with the rest of the application.

The changes integrate seamlessly with the existing codebase by following established patterns: using the existing translation system, reusing UI components from the modules directory, and maintaining the same styling approach with Tailwind CSS. The navigation now provides better context awareness with settings access directly from the switchers, reducing the number of clicks needed to access common configuration pages. The addition of proper accessibility attributes and keyboard navigation support ensures the enhanced navigation is usable by all users.
